PullRequest.Title: agentHost: honor SSH ProxyJump when connecting
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #317445

## Problem

Agent Host resolves effective OpenSSH configuration with `ssh -G`, but did not carry `ProxyJump` into the `ssh2` connection. A host reachable only through its configured jump host was therefore dialed directly from the Agents window and failed with `ENOTFOUND` or `EHOSTUNREACH`, while native OpenSSH and Remote SSH succeeded against the same config.

## Change

Preserve the resolved `ProxyJump` value through initial and reconnect configuration. For a single jump host, start native OpenSSH with `BatchMode=yes` and `-W`, pass its standard streams to `ssh2` through `ConnectConfig.sock`, and stop the owned helper when the SSH connection closes. The destination is passed after `--` so a config-derived value can never be read as an `ssh` option.

The jump alias, not a pre-resolved hostname, is handed to OpenSSH, so the jump host's own `HostName`, `User`, `Port` and `IdentityFile` still apply. Final-host authentication, host-key verification, Agent Host bootstrap and WebSocket handling are untouched.

Single-hop only. Comma-separated chains, `ProxyCommand`, interactive jump-host authentication, askpass IPC and `HostKeyAlias` behavior are unchanged, and there are no dependency, build or pipeline changes.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client`, `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, full `eslint`, and hygiene on the changed files — all clean
- Focused `vs/platform/agentHost/test/{common,node}` suite — 5245 passing. Unpatched `main` control runs the same suite at 5237 passing with the same two pre-existing `CopilotAgent` failures, so those are unrelated to this change.
- Live built Code OSS A/B, captured on commit `dca870d` (base `7b763e653ee2`), using disposable profiles, real key-authenticated jump and target SSH servers, and the actual Agent Host WebSocket relay:
  - Native OpenSSH reached `proxyjump-target.invalid:2222` through the configured jump host.
  - Unpatched `main` used the same Agents UI action, dialed the target directly, failed with `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`, and never contacted the jump or target servers.
  - Patched Code OSS contacted the jump, forwarded to the target, authenticated, launched the real Agent Host, and completed the SSH-forwarded WebSocket connection.
  - A direct-host control completed the same Agent Host flow without starting a jump helper.
  - All owned helper and Agent Host processes exited after the UI closed.
- The `--` terminator was added after that run, so this revision is not byte-identical to the Electron-tested one and the Electron harness was not re-run. It is covered separately: against OpenSSH 9.5p2, `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -W target.invalid:22 -V` prints the version and exits 0, while the same command with `-- -V` treats it as a hostname and exits 255; ordinary `host` and `user@host` destinations are unaffected. A unit regression asserts `--` is always immediately before the destination, and it fails without the production change.

Scenarios.Scenario: User connects from the Agents UI to a configured direct SSH host without ProxyJump.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The renderer resolves the alias, stages the configuration, and waits for the main-process connection. Existing `ssh -G` resolution, ssh2 network handshake, remote platform probes, CLI installation check, endpoint discovery, and relay setup remain on the critical path; the new proxy transport returns immediately without spawning anything.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Renderer-to-main calls to resolve SSH configuration and establish the connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolve request and one staged connection request per coalesced user connect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC sequence existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both must complete before the UI receives a usable connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `ssh -G <alias>` to resolve effective OpenSSH configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process per fresh configured-host resolution; no cache, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one-per-resolution subprocess ran before the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: ssh2 connects directly to the target and performs existing remote exec/relay setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SSH transport per fresh logical host connection, followed by a bounded sequence of existing remote commands on that transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Direct hosts used the same ssh2 transport and bootstrap sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Handshake and bootstrap must complete before the host is usable.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One logical host connection. Repeated clicks/retry requests for the same normalized address are coalesced by `RemoteAgentHostService._pendingConnects`; active connections are keyed and reused.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one in-flight dial per normalized address through the browser service. Different hosts can connect independently, as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved SSH config is not cached and `ssh -G` runs for each fresh connect/reconnect, unchanged by the diff. The active main-process `_connections` map reuses an established SSH client; relay-only reconnects reuse that client.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new guard requires both `sshConfigHost` and `proxyJump`, so direct configurations do not call `cp.spawn`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote bootstrap duration varies by target and whether the CLI is already installed, but the diff adds no work on this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: direct-host execution and boundary cardinality are unchanged apart from carrying one optional string.

Scenarios.Scenario: User establishes a fresh Agent Host connection to a target whose resolved SSH config contains one ProxyJump.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing `ssh -G` resolution and auth-attempt preparation, the main process starts one native OpenSSH `ssh -W` helper. Its spawn and jump-host/target forwarding are on the handshake critical path, and the existing ssh2 handshake plus remote bootstrap run over the helper's stdio.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `ssh -G <target alias>` to obtain the resolved target, identity, and ProxyJump settings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subprocess per fresh configured-host resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resolution subprocess ran, but its ProxyJump value was discarded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the ProxyJump transport can be constructed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start native OpenSSH with `BatchMode=yes -W target:port -- jump` and use its stdin/stdout as ssh2's socket.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one long-lived helper per fresh coalesced SSH session with a supported single-hop ProxyJump.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No helper was started; ssh2 attempted a direct target connection, so ProxyJump-only targets failed instead of establishing a session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The process must spawn and establish forwarding before ssh2 can complete its handshake; it remains the session transport afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the jump-host SSH connection and forward one byte stream to the resolved target; ssh2 then authenticates to the target over that stream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One jump connection and one forwarded target stream per fresh logical session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The target was dialed directly and the supported ProxyJump-only scenario could not progress.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds the required network hop to make progress for hosts that are not directly reachable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the existing target-side platform probes, CLI check/install, endpoint discovery, liveness filtering, and relay setup over the established SSH client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same bounded bootstrap sequence per fresh session; endpoint checks scale with discovered endpoint count as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operations followed successful direct SSH handshakes; ProxyJump-only hosts previously never reached them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing bootstrap remains on the connection critical path after the tunnel succeeds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One helper and one forwarded transport per fresh, effectively deduplicated host connection, not per authentication attempt, endpoint, message, or remote command.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-address connect requests are coalesced before reaching the factory. Connections to distinct configured hosts can each own one helper concurrently, matching independent user sessions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no transport cache across fully closed SSH sessions. While connected, the main `_connections` map retains and reuses the single SSH client/helper; reconnecting only the WebSocket relay does not spawn another helper. Stderr retention is capped at 4096 characters and keeps only the tail.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed guard, single `cp.spawn`, assignment to `ConnectConfig.sock`, same-address coalescing, and active-connection reuse directly establish cardinality and lifetime.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: OpenSSH startup and extra-hop latency depend on host configuration and network topology. This is intentional, restricted to ProxyJump-configured hosts, and replaces a failed direct dial rather than slowing a previously successful supported path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added subprocess and network hop are necessary to enable the requested scenario, remain one-per-session, and are not multiplied by auth attempts, endpoint count, or protocol messages.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatic or user-initiated reconnect and teardown of a ProxyJump-backed Agent Host.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every reconnect first performs the pre-existing `ssh -G`. If the main service still owns the SSH client, `connect(..., replaceRelay=true)` replaces only the relay and reuses the existing proxy helper. If the SSH session has closed, a fresh coalesced dial creates one new helper. Teardown destroys streams immediately; process-tree termination is fire-and-forget and off the reconnect/UI critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per reconnect invocation that reaches the main service; duplicate same-address dials are coalesced at the browser layer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reconnect already resolved SSH config with one subprocess.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks deciding whether to reuse or establish the connection, as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a new `ssh -W` helper only when no active SSH connection exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for warm relay-only reconnect; one for a cold/fresh reconnect attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold reconnect attempted direct ssh2 networking and warm relay reconnect reused the existing direct SSH client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold reconnect waits for helper spawn and forwarding; warm relay reconnect does not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Terminate the owned OpenSSH helper process tree when its ssh2 client closes or connection setup fails.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one kill operation for each still-running owned helper due to the `disposed` guard; none when the helper has already exited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no native proxy helper requiring process cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Stream destruction is synchronous, while `killTree` is intentionally not awaited and therefore does not block connection close or retry progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active helper per live SSH session and at most one in-flight reconnect per normalized address. Failed fresh handshakes are bounded by the existing 30-second handshake deadline (or interactive timeout while a prompt is open).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The browser service joins duplicate reconnect requests through `_pendingConnects`; retries for one address are sequential. Different addresses may reconnect concurrently and each can own one helper.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The active connection map is the warm-session cache: relay reconnection preserves the SSH client and proxy helper. A cold reconnect resolves config again and creates a fresh helper. Diagnostic stderr remains capped; no history accumulates across sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for normal connect, retry, and disposal paths: coalescing and connection reuse are explicit, and helper disposal is idempotent and registered on socket/client failure and close.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: OS process-tree termination cost varies by platform, but it is once per still-running helper and off the critical path. Parent shutdown behavior outside normal connection disposal was not directly exercised in repository tests, though normal close/error ownership is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: warm reconnect avoids repeated helper creation, cold retries are coalesced and bounded, and helper lifetime plus diagnostic memory are explicitly capped.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. Traced initial direct connections, fresh ProxyJump sessions, reconnect reuse/retry behavior, subprocess/network cardinality, stderr retention, and helper cleanup. The only new expensive work is one required OpenSSH forwarding helper per supported ProxyJump session plus bounded asynchronous cleanup; no actionable diff-introduced performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
